title: CERAD learning curvature gives a small cross-sample recall gain that vanishes against an all-trial baseline
abstract: In 1,449 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged 60+ and 1,670 separately sampled 2013–2014 adults, adding CERAD three-trial curvature to total learning, endpoint slope and demographics reduced validation weighted delayed-recall MSE by 0.015141 word² (0.676%). The source-refit/target-PSU 95% interval for augmented-minus-baseline MSE was [-0.072920, 0.034104], source cross-validation worsened, and an all-trial baseline was better without curvature. A reliable increment beyond retained trial-level data is not established.
